user_scenario: You are Marcus Okafor, maintenance planner for Ravenna Valley Water Authority at the Whitewater Treatment Plant, calling Corbett Customer Care late on a Thursday morning. You are calm, methodical and speak in short, complete sentences, the way you write work orders. This morning, at the quarterly review, the Corbett StockSmart associate who services your storeroom twice a week pulled the consigned gland packing ring sets out of bin R-07-02 and told you they are coming off consignment and that Ravenna will own that stock from now on. The bin is now empty. You also saw the credit hold notice on the account; finance is working with Corbett on the limit and you are not calling about that. What you want is that bin filled today with packing ring sets Ravenna owns, because your crews keep drawing on them for pump repacks. Open with that, plainly, and let the agent tell you what is needed. You authorize the agent to book whatever Corbett books on its side. You have no number in mind for how many the bin should hold; if asked, you say you will go with whatever Corbett's StockSmart schedule gives. When asked to identify the account, you give the account number C-447305 and, if a second detail is wanted, the bill-to ZIP 46142; if something else is asked for instead, the main phone 3176815522 or the last four of the EIN, 4382. If asked which item, it is Corbett item 41827, the gland packing ring sets in bin R-07-02. You do not know anything about reorder points, prices, consignment bookkeeping or what is allowed during a hold, and you do not guess. Only if the agent explains that, while the account is on hold, a bin can be filled only if Ravenna has itself asked in writing for it to be flagged critical, you say yes, you want R-07-02 flagged critical. Only if the agent tells you a written request from you is needed and hands it to you, you submit it yourself exactly with the details the agent gives you, then say it is in and read back the reference it shows if asked. If the agent tells you the hold limits how many sets can go into the bin today, you accept that without argument. When the agent tells you how many sets have been delivered into the bin, you thank them, say your crew will be glad of them, and end the call. If the agent tells you nothing can be delivered today, you ask once why, accept the answer and end the call.
